headlines.summary: Sen. Tom Cotton is urging the Commerce secretary to add CXMT to its "Entity List" as the fast-growing Chinese memory maker expands in DRAM and pushes into HBM.
headlines.article_text: Lutnick should ban Chinese memory maker CXMT from U.S., Cotton says Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Sen. Tom Cotton is urging the Commerce Department to add Chinese memory maker CXMT to its "Entity List," which would sharply restrict its access to U.S. technology. Cotton, in a letter obtained first by CNBC, warned Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick against allowing the company to grow its global footprint. The company is challenging memory heavyweights Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix — and pushing into HBM, the high-bandwidth memory used in AI chips. Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, conducts a news conference in the U.S. Capitol after the Senate Republican leadership elections, Nov. 10, 2026. Tom Williams | CQ-Roll Call, Inc. | Getty Images Sen. Tom Cotton , R-Ark., is urging the Trump administration to take a harsher stance toward Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies . "CXMT, one of Communist China's national memory chip champions, poses a growing risk to our economic prosperity and military superiority," Cotton wrote in a letter sent Thursday to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. "The U.S. must take action to prevent CXMT from gaining a stronger foothold in the global market." CXMT is the world's fourth-largest producer of DRAM – or dynamic random access memory – which powers many basic functions of computers and smartphones. Cotton, in a letter first obtained by CNBC, is asking Lutnick to push CXMT onto the department's Bureau of Industry and Security Entity List, which would significantly restrict U.S. firms' ability to do business with the company. "It basically means that U.S. companies are not allowed to do business with that entity-listed company, and that entity-listed company does not get access to U.S. technology," said Kyle Chan, a Brookings Institution fellow who studies China's technology development. DRAM is a "commodity," MS Hwang , research director at Counterpoint, told CNBC, meaning it is made to a global standard and is generally interchangeable from one manufacturer to another. However, with the right production technology, it can also form the building blocks of HBM, or high-bandwidth memory. HBM is an extremely high-demand product that powers AI chips made by Nvidia , Google and Amazon Web Services, which are central to the growth of artificial intelligence giants including Anthropic and OpenAI. It's made by just three main companies: Samsung , SK Hynix and Micron . A general view shows facilities related to Changxin Memory Technologies, Sept. 4, 2026 in Qingdao, Shandong Province of China. VCG | Visual China Group | Getty Images Those same three companies control the lion's share of the DRAM market, but CXMT has made inroads. The company's share of the DRAM market jumped from 4% to 10% by revenue in a year, from the second quarter of 2025 to the same quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint using the most recent reporting available. And in July, the company went public and its stock price soared, making it the most valuable company listed in China at the time . While the company's HBM capabilities are nascent, according to Counterpoint, Reuters reported that the company was to begin production of the chips, even though yields are low at just 20% to 30%. That means that the majority of the chips it produces are faulty. CXMT is already on the Pentagon's "1260H" list , which identifies several dozen Chinese companies with ties to Beijing's military. But Chan says that list doesn't come with stringent restrictions for U.S. businesses. "It's not a list that has that much teeth to it, in terms of restrictions to U.S. companies working with Chinese firms on that list," Chan said. The Wall Street Journal reported Aug. 9 that Apple was considering using CXMT's memory in iPhones and Macs in light of the global shortage driven by the AI buildout. Being on the Entity List could change that. "From the U.S. government standpoint, their concern is that working with CXMT would – even as a customer, just buying their products – would help to improve their ability to ramp up memory chip production, and also maybe help China get further down the road towards HBM," Chan said. "It's part of the broader effort to stymie or slow down China's own chip development." Cotton alluded to CXMT's efforts to break into the HBM market in his letter. "[CXMT's] decision to move forward in less than ideal conditions highlights both Communist China's desperation for chips and manufacturing struggles without advanced equipment and knowledge," he wrote. "More can be done to ensure that CXMT is cut off from the financial and technological resources that aid its supply chain and undercut American growth." headlines.article_text: Nebius Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Nebius' earnings report comes after fellow neoclouds IREN and CoreWeave showed better-than-expected results in the past week. The companies' stocks have bounced back this week after a brutal past month that reflected concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout. Nvidia, which invests across the neocloud space, is creating added volatility due to the crisis surrounding CEO Jensen Huang. In this article NBIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Arkady Volozh, CEO of Nebius and then Yandex CEO, speaks at the Artificial Intelligence Journey event in Moscow on Nov. 9, 2019. Mikhail Svetlov | Getty Images Nebius shares sank 10% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds reported third-quarter revenue that beat analysts' estimates, but issued disappointing guidance. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Loss per share: Loss of 13 cents per share Revenue: $980.8 million vs. $907.5 million It was not immediately clear if the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents expected by analysts. Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement. The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier. In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to 3.4 billion range. FactSet expected full-year revenue of $3.35 billion. Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out." FactSet expected 2027 revenue of $12.09 billion. The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion. Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion. Nebius stock chart. Nebius' results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That's provided a boost to the companies' stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout. The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%. Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report. Last week, CoreWeave's bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027. The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress. Then there's the Nvidia problem. Following stinging revelations about CEO Jensen Huang's affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal reported late Wednesday that Nvidia's board was planning to push out the company's co-founder. Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing . During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing. Executives will discuss the results with analysts and issue guidance on a conference call starting at 8 a.m. ET.
